reviewedBy: Claude Code session that authored the scrollable-table keyboard fix (not a cold reviewer, not a human)
method: Agent-run Playwright keyboard walk in Chrome 154 against the local analytics stack (synthetic data, operator session), 2026-10-05, at 1440x1000 and 390x844, light scheme. Sections walked: overview, albums, albums with compare=publication_age, photos in table view, sources, measurement, plus /analytics/sites; every details element opened. Before the edit, on main f640e94: 7 table regions rendered and none took Tab focus (6 had tabIndex -1, Album comparison table had no tabindex); axe scrollable-region-focusable flagged only 3 of the 7 at 390, so it was not the gate. After the edit: all 7 took Tab focus with a computed 3px outer ring at both widths, and at 390 ArrowRight increased scrollLeft on each; axe reported 0. The ring was screenshotted for the first focused region in each section at both widths. Walked: Album comparison table, First N days after publication, Daily comparison from publication, Popular, rising, and recently active photos, Recorded event counts, Which album rankings change, Traffic classification correction history. Checked in source only, because they did not render locally: Search and download evidence (no diagnostic rows), Version 2 correction history (no v2 corrections), Tagged arrival actions (source provider unavailable; tabindex unchanged from main), Actions by page on /analytics/sites (report unavailable locally), and Daily activity (inside .legacy-trend, hidden by an unconditional display:none rule). Not covered: a screen-reader pass, a human keyboard walk, a physical device, a cold reviewer.
scope: Analytics operator scrollable tables (keyboard focus, labels, focus ring)
